analysis:
All changed units in this batch are test-only files under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Autopilot/. They add a fixture (AutopilotPlacementFixture.swift lines 120-126: two *ForTesting setters for autopilotResidentSince and autopilotLeaseUntil), a shared recovery fixture (SelectedModelRecoveryFixture.swift) and four test suites for selected-model recovery. They contain no production code, so no runtime trust boundary, key, attestation, encryption or prefix-cache storage behavior changes here. The tests use scripted memory, stub engines, temp directories, and a loopback placeholder coordinator URL (ws://127.0.0.1:0/unused), and pass attestationSigner nil. None of this reaches production configuration.

The tests do describe security-relevant availability policy that lives in unseen production code: recovery pauses on add-on hold or drain (TB-012/T-059; anAddonHoldCancelsTheAttemptInProgress), honors Autopilot holds, leases and pins, and never evicts models in the running daemon's selection. The recovery load is cancelled when an add-on hold begins, so no model loads beside the add-on's VMs. I could not verify that the production code implements these behaviors. The production selected-model recovery and release logic (ProviderLoop, SelectedModelRecovery) was not supplied.

Open question for integration: the production commit paired with these tests should be reviewed for (a) the release/eviction policy for busy adopted models (stops new requests, drains in-flight, then evicts), which affects A-018 availability and in-flight consumer requests (A-001); (b) whether recovery loads honor the add-on hold fence (T-059); (c) whether the recovery attempt state exposed through daemon state leaks only model IDs and blockers. No findings from the test-only diff.
